explanation: Cane sugar was a costly import, sold by apothecaries as a spice and medicine. It became cheap through Caribbean plantations worked by enslaved Africans.

claims.text: Honey was the main sweetener in medieval Europe before cane sugar became widely available.
Maple syrup and agave syrup are products of the Americas, unknown in medieval Europe, and date syrup was a Middle Eastern sweetener; none was medieval Europe's main sweetener.
In medieval Europe, cane sugar was an expensive import, often sold by apothecaries as a spice and a medicine.
Sugar became cheap and plentiful through plantations in the Caribbean that used the forced labour of enslaved Africans.
